pr.title: Tell agents with the Projector plugin to build every change with implement
pr.head: f994a630cb21bd945d3fdee160aad5d597af8770

summary: When a repository adopts Projector, project init writes a section into its AGENTS.md, the instructions file Codex reads (and Claude Code reads through CLAUDE.md, which links to it). The section sits between two HTML-comment markers, carries a version number, and comes from a template that ships with the CLI. When the template changes, project check warns that a repository's copy is outdated, and project init rewrites only the text between the markers.

Before this change, that section mentioned the implement skill only for stacked pull requests. A session that built a change some other way still opened a draft pull request, but it skipped implement's hand-over, the last step where implement opens the pull request and starts a fix loop that answers review findings as they arrive. Findings then sat until someone noticed, as happened on #270.
Version 5 of the template does two things:

1. It adds the implement rule. Build every change you will open a pull request for with implement, whether it follows a plan or only a description, however small.
  2. It makes the plugin-dependent rules conditional. The new rule and the existing rule to open every pull request as a draft move into a ### Projector skills subsection that applies only when the Projector plugin's skills are available. A contributor without the plugin has no review loop of their own to mark a draft ready, so following the draft rule would leave every pull request in draft.

The rules about where plans live, the project command, the writing style, and stacks stay unconditional. The note saying Projector generates the section moves to its top, so it no longer reads as part of the new subsection.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Block: the generated section between <!-- projector:begin N --> and <!-- projector:end -->, where N is the template's version.
  • Hand-over: implement's last step, which opens a draft pull request and starts or joins a fix loop on it.
  • Fix loop: start-fix-loop, which runs fix-pr on each pull request it watches whenever a review leaves findings.

cards.html: One review, of f994a63: clean, with no finding threads. It suggests rewrapping one short line in docs/cli.md.

groups.title: The version 5 template
groups.kicker: The text project init writes into every adopting repository
intro: This is the source of the change. project init renders it by replacing {projects_dir} with the repository's plans directory, usually docs/projects, and the first line's version number tells project check whether a repository's copy is current.
The diff moves the draft paragraph, unchanged, from the unconditional part into the new subsection, and adds the plugin condition and the implement paragraph above it.

files.note: The template itself: version bumped to 5, generation note moved to the top, and a new ### Projector skills subsection at the end.

checks.text: The rule agrees with skills/implement/SKILL.md: implement accepts a plan or a plain description, ends at gh pr create --draft, and starts or joins a fix loop from the top-level conversation unless fix.auto_start is false. Checked by reading its "Start from a description" and "Hand the work over" sections.
Both invocations match how docs/plugins.md and README.md say each host calls a plugin skill: /projector:<skill> in Claude Code and $<skill> in Codex.
An agent decides whether this subsection applies by whether it can see Projector's skills. Without them, everything above the heading still applies.

files.note: Pins the SHA-256 of the version 5 template, so a later edit that forgets to bump the version fails the test.

groups.kicker: This repository's AGENTS.md and the CLI reference follow the template
intro: Projector uses its own convention, so its AGENTS.md carries the same block, refreshed by project init. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it, so Claude Code reads the same text. docs/cli.md describes what init writes, and now says which part of the block depends on the plugin.
